clue.text: Fishing adviser said cat must go back — it takes fish

indicators.note: said tells us to take the sound of the adviser's title rather than its spelling

parts.note: a gillie (or ghillie) is a Scottish attendant who guides anglers and hunters

indicators.note: must go back tells us the word for a cat is read from right to left

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A fishing guide complains that a fish-stealing cat must be sent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must go back' turns TOM into MOT. The first syllable of the seabird is pronounced like GILLIE, a Highland fishing guide.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a diving seabird of the auk family that lives on a diet of fish.

clue.text: Cousin of ours sending fruit round to consume

indicators.note: round means the fruit's letters go around the other word

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
eat means consume

explanation.surface: A relative sends fruit around for people to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas, chimpanzees and orangutans are close primate relatives of humans.

clue.text: Italian footballers start off season

indicators.note: start off means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: winter is a season

explanation.surface: Italian football players kick off the season.
explanation.walkthrough: Inter Milan is a major Italian football club, usually called Inter.
explanation.definitionFit: Internazionale of Milan is a leading Serie A club, known simply as Inter.

clue.text: Ignores evidence of spring

definitions.meaning: trees putting out new foliage show that spring has come

explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to skip it; new foliage on trees is a sign of spring.

clue.text: Ruin depressed English playwright

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
low means depressed

explanation.surface: An English dramatist sinks into gloom and ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was an Elizabethan dramatist, author of Doctor Faustus.

clue.text: Muscle from dinosaur missing middle section

indicators.note: missing middle section says a central chunk is cut out of the dinosaur's name

parts.note: the triceratops is a three-horned dinosaur

explanation.surface: Muscle tissue from a dinosaur with its midriff missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing middle section' removes RATO from the middle of TRICERATOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the large three-headed muscle at the back of the upper arm.

clue.text: Fruit pulp — oh, no!

parts.note: pap is soft mushy food, a pulp
aw is an exclamation of disappointment or dismay

explanation.surface: Someone finds their fruit has gone to mush and groans.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaw (pawpaw) is a tropical fruit, another name for the papaya.

clue.text: Singer is favourite around ladies' organisation

indicators.note: around means the favourite's letters surround the organisation's

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
the WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's community organisation

explanation.surface: A favourite vocalist performs for a women's group.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a British women's society famous for jam-making. The singer is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pewit or lapwing is a bird, and crosswords often call any bird a singer.

clue.text: King penguin originally fed outside old shelter

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the bird's name

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
ate means fed; outside says it sits beyond the old shelter, after it in the answer

explanation.surface: A king penguin is fed beyond an old shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes P from penguin. 'outside' only says the word for fed stands beyond the old shelter, i.e. after it, so the pieces run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a monarch or ruler with great power.

clue.text: Used to be inexperienced, raising capital

indicators.note: raising, in a down clue, means the letters are read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: was means used to be
raw means inexperienced, as in a raw recruit

explanation.surface: A novice used to be good at raising capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns the whole run WASRAW upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital city of Poland.

clue.text: Tear off to secure Times special edition

indicators.note: to secure means the outer letters hold something fast within them
off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: x is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Someone rips out a page from a special issue of The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TEAR to ETRA, and 'to secure' puts X inside it. The surface leans on the newspaper itself, but Times here is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is an additional issue of a newspaper printed for breaking news.

clue.text: Collection available after fall, not in spring

definitions.text: Collection available after fall, not in spring

parts.words: Collection available after fall, not in spring
parts.note: fall reads as a season but means a shower from the sky; spring reads as a season but means a source welling from the ground, and this water is gathered from the sky instead

explanation.surface: Something to be collected in autumn rather than in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Fall and spring look like seasons; they are a downpour and a natural water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Water caught in butts after a shower comes from the sky, unlike water rising from a spring.

clue.text: Hull's the target for this missile

definitions.text: Hull's the target for this missile

parts.words: Hull's the target for this missile
parts.note: Hull looks like the English city on the Humber, but it is the body of a ship, which an underwater weapon is aimed at

explanation.surface: A missile is aimed at the city of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull, capitalised as the first word, suggests the Yorkshire port; it is a ship's hull.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater weapon is launched to strike a ship below the waterline.

clue.text: State school, one with a place for son inside

indicators.note: inside, with a place for, says one letter is accommodated within the school's name

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
i is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A state school finds room for a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the famous English boarding school near Windsor; S goes inside it to give ESTON, then I and A follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, a sovereign nation or state.

clue.text: Men, locked together in conflict

parts.note: locked together seems to describe men grappling in battle, but means captured soldiers held in confinement during hostilities

explanation.surface: Soldiers grappling with each other in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Locked together suggests hand-to-hand combat; read it as men locked up during a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Captured servicemen held by the enemy during hostilities are kept locked up together in camps.

clue.text: It can clarify how vocalist introduces himself to girl?

parts.note: a singer might say 'I sing' to explain who he is
lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A singer chats up a young woman by saying what he does.
explanation.walkthrough: Isinglass, a fish gelatin, is used to clear beer and wine of sediment.
explanation.definitionFit: This gelatin from fish bladders is used as a fining agent to make beer and wine clear.

clue.text: Spike becoming heartless and showing impatience

parts.note: a fid is a tapered spike used by sailors to splice rope

indicators.note: heartless means one of the central letters is removed

parts.note: getting means becoming, as in getting old

explanation.surface: A spiky character turns cold and grows impatient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes one central T from GETTING. A fid is a sailor's tool, a pointed spike for opening rope strands.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless fiddling movements are a sign of being impatient.

clue.text: One Creakle caned often having to lift bottom right up and spread legs apart

indicators.text: having to lift bottom right up
indicators.note: in a down entry this says the bottom letter is lifted all the way to the top

parts.note: in Dickens's David Copperfield, schoolmaster Creakle repeatedly canes the pupil Tommy Traddles

explanation.surface: A Dickensian schoolboy must bend over and take a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: Creakle is the brutal headmaster in David Copperfield; Traddles is the boy he canes most. 'having to lift bottom right up' moves the last S to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit or stand with one leg on either side of something is to have the legs spread wide apart.

clue.text: Constitutional reform leaving many questions unanswered

definitions.text: Constitutional reform leaving many questions unanswered

parts.words: Constitutional reform leaving many questions unanswered
parts.note: a change to the US Constitution lets a witness decline to answer questions that might incriminate them

explanation.surface: A constitutional change that has left lots of issues unresolved.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a poorly drafted reform; in fact the US amendment protects the right to stay silent rather than incriminate oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: This US constitutional provision protects against self-incrimination, so witnesses invoking it refuse to reply.

clue.text: Protested scripture was not infallible

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible
erred means made a mistake, was not infallible

explanation.surface: Someone objected that the Bible was capable of error.
explanation.walkthrough: Protested here means declared firmly, as in 'protested his innocence', not objected.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest one's innocence is to declare it firmly, which is to assert.

clue.text: Wit from English, stock examples

parts.note: pigs and rams are examples of livestock
a ram is another kind of farm stock

explanation.surface: Humour drawn from stock English examples.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock means livestock here, not stock phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a brief clever saying, a piece of wit.

clue.text: For such a good meal, drink outside and drink inside

indicators.note: outside, with inside later, says the first drink wraps round the second

parts.note: to sup is to drink
to lap is to drink, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Drinking both outdoors and indoors makes for a fine feast.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'outside' and 'inside' signal the container, said from each drink's point of view. Slap-up is British informal for lavish.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a lavish, first-rate spread of food.

clue.text: What traveller carries in toboggan is a joke

indicators.note: in places the joke within the word for the sled

parts.note: a luge is a light racing toboggan
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Someone sledding with a toboggan finds it amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags and cases are what a passenger takes along on a journey.

clue.text: Fittingly put to use after change of heart

indicators.note: change of heart means the middle letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: apply means to put to use

explanation.surface: Something is put to fit use once someone changes their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' swaps the central P of APPLY for T.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptly means in a suitable or appropriate way.

clue.text: I, holding degree, understand a Japanese art form

indicators.note: holding means one word clasps another within it

parts.note: ken means to know or understand, Scots and dialect
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A graduate claims to grasp a traditional Japanese art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' signals the container. Ken is Scots for know or understand, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the traditional Japanese craft of arranging flowers.

clue.text: Getting on, making name in a band's performance

indicators.note: in places the name's abbreviation inside the performance

parts.note: a gig is a live performance by a band

explanation.surface: An ageing musician still makes a name in a band's concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing old.

clue.text: Complicated, art repels mural craftsman

indicators.note: complicated suggests the letters are tangled up, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Intricate artwork puts off someone working on a wall painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complicated' rearranges ART and REPELS.
explanation.definitionFit: A plasterer is a tradesman who coats walls, mural here meaning relating to walls.

clue.text: Clung to by climber, I struggled

parts.note: vied means competed or struggled

explanation.surface: A mountaineer recalls fighting hard while clinging to a rock face.
explanation.walkthrough: The scanned clue lacks the I the wordplay needs. The climber is a plant, not a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall covered with the evergreen climbing plant is one clung to by that creeper.

clue.text: Forcing oneself forward to back up throw

indicators.note: to back says the little word next to it is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a shy is a throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: Someone throws something to support a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' turns UP into PU.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushy describes someone who asserts themselves too forcefully.

clue.text: Mob leader expected to accept point put by giant

indicators.note: to accept means the outer word takes the others in

parts.note: due means expected, as in a train due at noon
e is east, a compass point
Magog is a legendary giant, paired with Gog

explanation.surface: A gang boss is expected to take advice from a huge man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' signals the container. Gog and Magog are legendary giants of British folklore, whose effigies stand in London's Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: A demagogue is a rabble-rouser who leads the crowd by appeals to passion.
